primitives.name: Feasibility Ceiling
primitives.verbatim_quote: Equations & assumptions - Feasibility ceiling: selective accuracy ≤ min(1, p/c), where p = base accuracy, c = coverage.
primitives.assumptions: Predictor must have known base accuracy p and coverage c; selective accuracy is bounded by worst-case ratio.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When p/c > 1, selective accuracy caps at 1 regardless of performance.

layer2.mapping: GSE uses this bound to preclude projects exceeding theoretical limits without tuning; acts as a prior constraint on decision thresholds.
layer2.telemetry: Base hit-rate and coverage ratio computed from validation set.

primitives.name: Score Decomposition
primitives.verbatim_quote: 3): each candidate's score = a case-level component shared across candidates + a candidate-specific residual; the top-two *margin* cancels the shared component, so it reads "which candidate is correct" from the residual gap — while the *top score* retains case-level information ("is any answer present?").
primitives.latex: s_i = a(x) + r_i \quad \text{and} \quad \text{margin} = s_1 - s_2 = r_1 - r_2
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'s_i': 'scalar score for candidate i', 'a(x)': 'shared case-level term', 'r_i': 'residual for candidate i'}
primitives.assumptions: Scores are additive in a shared and residual structure; margin isolates relative differences.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When a(x) dominates, margin loses discriminative power; top-score preserves presence signal.

layer2.mapping: GSE models score as sum of global context and local evidence; margin enables alternative-focused decision-making.
layer2.telemetry: Residual variance and top-score stability across ranked candidates.

primitives.name: Margin vs Top-Score Gate
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Proposition 1: two joint laws with identical unlabeled score distributions P_S and identical base accuracy, but margin-vs-top-score gains of opposite sign (+1/2 vs -1/2 in the construction) — so no unlabeled-score functional identifies the better gate.
primitives.latex: \text{No functional of } P_S \text{ distinguishes margin vs top-score effectiveness}
primitives.assumptions: Unlabeled score distributions are identical; effectiveness depends on labeled outcome structure.
primitives.breakdown_regime: In absence of labeled data, no statistical test can determine superior gating strategy.

layer2.mapping: GSE must empirically validate margin vs top-score efficacy through controlled experiments; not derivable from score alone.
layer2.telemetry: Empirical comparison of margin vs top-score performance on held-out cases.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that in selective prediction, scores decompose into a shared case-level component and a residual. The margin between top two scores cancels the shared term, isolating relative correctness. This allows for a more robust decision rule than relying on absolute score magnitude. The feasibility ceiling provides a hard limit on achievable selective accuracy based on base accuracy and coverage. No unlabeled score distribution can distinguish which gate—margin or top-score—is better, necessitating empirical validation. These primitives enable GSE to pre-screen projects and choose optimal decision criteria based on domain-specific constraints.
